reviews.text: Juper
Its pretty good.

If you do not know the legendary DRL: when roguelike developers were mostly making huge, extremely complex, 20+ hour long games, DRL was a relatively simple one with short runs, so Spelunky and all short rogueish games basically take from it. Out of the short roguelikes, it is still the one I had the most fun with. DOOM but where you control the flow of time, with a great turn-based dodging system! And JHC is a greatly improved version of it. (version = based on the same engine, it is clearly a game on its own) Would love to have an option of the mini-map using ASCII.

Why does the game have a progression system? The first two runs on normal and hard were successful, and then I just have to waste time to unlock the fourth difficulty? There are too many annoying moments so far.

after about 4 runs over 10 hours, can safely say there's not near enough randomization or content to keep this interesting as a roguelike. I have only vague memories of DoomRL at this point, but I also dont remember paying for that one. Maybe better after a few major updates but until then I'd say pass

I so wanted to like this game. I love jupiter hell, and I was hyped for classic, especially as it promised to update jupiter hell (normal?) as well. But classic felt...bland. The mechanics lacked depth after Jupiter hell, the art generic or lacking, the enemies straight forward either easy or annhilatory hard to the point that certain set ups you walk out of a gate and die. I know creators are short of cash, and that the game was created to help with that. But classic just feels like a poor imitation of the game it was supposed to be based on. A waste a developer time which could have been spent improving the game which they already had or to make somthing entirely new.

Whereas Jupiter Hell was more like a fork of DRL going off in its own direction with its own new mechanics this is more like a continuation/ a new update for the original DRL with the licensed Doom serial numbers filed off obviously, don't wanna get sued after all. This puts it in a funny spot of being more DRL than the original DRL successor. But yes if you liked DRL you will like this. Because it's literally DRL lol. For me it was one of the first Rogue Likes I ever played and also coincided with the first time I really dove into Doom and its fan creations and ♥♥♥♥ (Wad's PK3's etc) so don't look to me for an objective analysis here. I'm biased and Rose tinted and I don't care.
If they make this control like the Jupiter hell before it, it would be great! If you play both games back and forth the control differences ruin it.

My initial impression is really good (I haven't really played any of the other titles). My only gripe here is that there isn't as much variety as most reviews suggest, since the vast majority of perks are simple +damage, +speed or +defensive options and the weapons (that I have found) aren't particularly inspired either. Not bad, by any means, but definitely a bit conservative in terms of skill/item design, as a lot of it is very grounded and to the point. The very first few floors are also very samey, to the point that this is the one thing that made me contemplate a negative review for the game, as the runs always start the exact same, pistol, shotgun, chain gun, grenade launcher, combat knife, the same green armor. Every. Time. So that becomes kind of a chore very quickly. I would love to see more "out there" upgrades and master skills in the future, or more involved weapons.

I preferred DRL over Jupiter Hell (not classic) so this was good to see in the works. For the uninitiated, this game is a very short, fast-paced traditional roguelike. No grinding, no hunger, one straight line to the bottom. I think some trad roguelike nerd site I read once called it a "coffee break" roguelike? I'd put each run at about an hour and a half at length if you win, so, I think that's shorter than even Shattered Pixel Dungeon gets, if you're familiar. I don't miss the pain mechanic at all, and I do prefer the pixel art artstyle and the previous game's talents, I just also did not miss being able to blow up loot with explosions (fireangel eating poorly in this house). The new special maps tend to have "it just kills you" mechanics you're not gonna know how to deal with the first time around - feels really bad when two different rooms I can think of off the top of my head start filling with lava unavoidably, and only find out in the graveyard file (should you know how to read it) that you were expected to run down a *different* corridor - and it's annoying to have to trial-and-error upgrade every single item in the game to have assemblies logged. The active abilities every class gets is kind of poorly tutorialized, I had to give the help page four reads through to find out what button it was.

Compared to the old freeware DRL, this is well on its way to differentiating itself into its own experience. Compared to the previous game Jupiter Hell, it's a lot faster paced and more arcadey, and a lot of the UI is stripped down for simplicity (perhaps a bit too far). Features are still being added but it's already quite good. Regardless of which game in the series you want to play, there's a ton of strategic depth, varied builds and challenge runs. The gun-focused turn based roguelike has a very unique feel that I haven't really seen from anyone else. Thanks to the challenge runs, the difficulty curve that stretches all the way from "manageable for anyone patient" to "very few human beings can beat this" for the hardest badges. Don't buy this expecting to 100% it easily!

Boring, ameteurish. Compared to other roguelikes it doesn't communicate the important information without requiring spoilers and wikis. Gigantic difficulty spike in dante that just has you raising your arms in confusion as to how the game expects you to deal with the incoming damage despite having 90 hp and insane armor and killing everything in 1-2 shots. (I am greater player in DCSS, a game that actually communicates how to deal with the challenges it has and rewards your build crafting by actually making you feel powerful). I was absolutely nuking everything that entered my screen before dante and then all the sudden I am taking 45 damage per hit with one guy on my screen. I look at him and his page shows nothing about what his attack does or how much damage it does or how to avoid it. Awful at show don't tell, the game requires you to play a tutorial to learn the rules of the game rather than teaching you them organically via gameplay. The monster and item screens are esoteric and unclear and don't give you enough information to be useful. There is little to no information in game that helps you understand what the various terms mean (Just absolutely lapped by DCSS here having a full lookup of every enemy and item in the game at a keystroke.) Probably won't play again. The first two third of the game is way too easy and boring with little decision making besides which guy to shoot first and which of the dumb masteries you are going to chain your character to for the rest of the game. And chaining the difficulty of your game to RNG ammo availability is just stupid. It ends up feeling like a slot machine half the time. Just a poorly made game. I honestly can't believe this has 20+ years of game dev put into it.

Comes with DRL as a designated mod in the steam workshop. For anyone who doesn't know what DRL is, it stands for Doom the Rogue-Like. DRL is a turn based, top down version of the original doom game. Jupiter Hell Classic is just a procedural roguelike version of DRL, with its own unique elements. Both Jupiter Hell Classic and DRL are great games.
